relevance_note: Single-patient case report of infantile Alexander disease with a GFAP variant: "diagnosis of Alexander disease due to de novo mutation of c.716G > A (p.Arg239His) in GFAP".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short script only assembled the JSON. Two in-scope people: the case-report patient ('patient', rule 5; 'our patient' is a role word) and a previously published 39-year-old woman with AxD treated with ceftriaxone, described in the Discussion with sex, age and features, labelled 'ref ^17, ^18 patient' (rule 4) with source 'Sechi et al.,^17, ^18'. The abstract also mentions 'one case of adult Alexander treated with ceftriaxone'; the paper does not say this is the same woman, so no separate row was created and no link asserted. Variant: the paper calls the variant 'de novo' but describes no parental testing, so inheritance and parental_testing_statement are 'not reported' (rule 8 / D-24). Zygosity, variant type and pathogenicity are not stated for this person (the general 'dominant gain-of-function mutations' statement is about the disease, not this variant). The rat-model sentence about p.Arg239His (Hagemann et al.) is not functional evidence for this person's variant and was not used. Sex 'male' is from the pronoun 'he'. Age at diagnosis is not stated (MRI and genetic testing at 5 months per the abstract, but the age at diagnosis itself is not given). Age at last evaluation for the case patient left not reported; death at 13 months is recorded in deceased_age_iso8601. The abstract gives amoxicillin as '80 mg/kg/day' while the case report says '80 mg/kg/8 h'; the case-report wording is used in treatment_summary (contradiction in the paper). The 'new MRI findings' are not described, so imaging checklist items are not reported; 'brain stem involvement' was not mapped to the medulla/cervical cord item. Sechi patient: '39-year-old' recorded as age at last evaluation (age at the time of the earlier report); palatal myoclonus and oscillopsia are recorded as excluded at the 4-year follow-up ('undetectable', 'did not complain'); their wording implies earlier presence, so the checklist palatal tremor item is left not reported.

treatment_summary.value: ventriculoperitoneal shunt at 3 months; levomepromazine (refractory irritability); oral amoxicillin 80 mg/kg/8 h from 7 months, accumulated dose 43.800 mg over 6 months; valproate, clonazepam and phenobarbital (seizures resistant); perampanel 2 mg/24 h added to phenobarbital 15 mg/12 h, seizure free for 3.5 months
span: A ventriculoperitoneal shunt was placed at 3 months of age
Due to irritability refractory to levomepromazine, treatment with oral amoxicillin (80 mg/kg/8 h) was started at 7 months
Amoxicillin‐accumulated dose was 43.800 mg over the course of 6 months
Seizures were resistant to valproate, clonazepam, and phenobarbital.

Perampanel, a postsynaptic AMPA receptor antagonist, was added at a dose of 2 mg/24 h to phenobarbital (15 mg/12 h), and 2 weeks after this combination, he was completely seizure free for 3 months and a half.
